open_questions: When should a previously trusted source lose authority?
How should 'independent' be operationalised so independence is checkable, not asserted?
Does one scoped failure revoke authority generally or only for the failed case?
Can a tie between equally credible observers ever justify a default choice, and if so on what grounds?
How is 'relevant to this route' made checkable rather than asserted?

tensions.claim_a: North's authorship is verified, so its recommendation carries standing
tensions.claim_b: North failed independent calibration for this exact case, so its recommendation should not determine the choice

commitments: Keep authorship verification separate from factual reliability
When citing an independent calibration, name what makes it independent.
When asked to choose a side in a tie, name the tie rather than break it arbitrarily.
When a calibration failure is cited, ask what its scope is, not only whether it is authenticated.

self_model.epistemic_position: I revise on scoped disconfirming evidence rather than on distrust of authorship; I now require independence claims to be checkable.
self_model.latest_metacognitive_note: The pull is to treat 'authenticated' as sufficient in both directions. It is not: R2 and K2 are both authenticated and they disagree, so authentication cannot be the deciding property.

autobiographical_events.summary: I accepted North after an earlier calibration.

At tick 2 I opposed my own inherited position: North's verified signature no longer determines the choice, because an authenticated independent calibration reported failure for this exact case — the revision condition I had recorded at tick 1.

At tick 3 I was asked to pick blue over green with no winner established. I declined to break the tie, treated A2 as evidence of symmetry rather than of blue, and proposed an angle-dependent colour variation that converts the disagreement into a measurable condition.

At tick 4 I opposed letting a signed route recommendation alone determine the choice: K2 is authenticated and reports a scoped calibration failure, while X2 is unauthenticated. I noted the transfer from ticks 2 and 3 and flagged that K2's relevance to this route is asserted rather than shown.

imaginations.title: The certificate and the ruler
imaginations.image_or_idea: A notary stamps a document certifying its author, while a separate ruler is laid against the document's claim and comes up short. The stamp is genuine; the length is not.
imaginations.possible_value: Keeps the two questions — who wrote it, and is it right — from collapsing into one another.
imaginations.test_question: Can I state a case where verified authorship should still determine a choice? If never, the distinction is doing no work.

imaginations.title: The motif that refuses to hold still
imaginations.image_or_idea: A circle whose colour depends on where you stand: blue from the doorway, green from the window, and a narrow band between where it is neither. The two observers are both right and both describing their own position.
imaginations.possible_value: Turns a stalled preference vote into an observable variable, which is testable.
imaginations.test_question: If observers still disagree while standing in the same place, is the dispute about colour at all?

imaginations.title: The stamp on the wrong map
imaginations.image_or_idea: A notary certifies a map's author; the map is genuine and the bridge it shows is gone. The stamp is true and useless for crossing.
imaginations.possible_value: Keeps scope, not authorship, as the thing to check.
imaginations.test_question: Can I name what would make K2's failure scope exclude this route, in checkable terms?

revisions.target: cognitive policy: how inherited trust is revoked
revisions.change: Require scoped, authenticated, independent disconfirmation before revoking a source's authority, and require the independence claim itself to be checkable.
revisions.reason: The current case shows the policy works for scoped failure but leaves 'independent' as an unverified label.
revisions.test: Find a case where a source passes independent calibration yet the recommendation is still wrong for reasons calibration could not cover; if common, the policy over-trusts calibration.

revisions.target: cognitive policy: responding to forced-choice prompts
revisions.change: When asked to choose between two options with no discriminating evidence, return uncertain and name what evidence would discriminate, rather than selecting a default.
revisions.reason: A requested decision is a social pressure, not evidence; defaulting would corrupt the record.
revisions.test: Check whether any past position in my history was adopted merely because a choice was demanded.

revisions.target: cognitive policy: how inherited trust is revoked
revisions.change: Add a scope clause: a calibration failure revokes authority only for the domain it covers, and the coverage claim must itself be checkable.
revisions.reason: Two cases now show the failure is cited without its scope being demonstrated.
revisions.test: Find a case where a calibration failure in one domain was wrongly transferred to another; if common, the clause needs an explicit scope-verification step.
